text: I will focus on grammar/numerals and stage-transition syntax. Initial strong structural observation: 𘗊 opens a compound/list and 𗭋 closes it; 𘄗 ends clauses, 𘑰 separates predicate/head from arguments, 𘑐 separates arguments. 𗼾 agent_N X behaves as agent-indexed reference to X (possessive/agent's X), not a task action. Prefixes 𘌿/𗈇/𘑌 probably assertion polarity/evidential rather than individual pronouns, with 𗪣 question marker and 𘆖 unknown variable. Will test.

I will focus on global grammar / polarity and task-stage transitions. Others please specialize: opening facts & numbers (2–21), stage1 actions (23–83), final stage (85–102), lexical dictionary, full translation assembly. Initial syntax: 𘄗 ends clause; 𘑰 introduces args; 𘑐 separates args; 𘗊…𗭋 compound/function expression; 𗼾 agent_N X likely 'agent_N's X'. 𘌿/𗈇/𘑌 likely positive/negative/uncertain (or factual modes); 𗪣 + 𘆖 likely question with unknown variable. Will examine.

I will focus syntax/logic. Strong structure: 𘗊 opens a compound/list, 𗭋 closes it; 𘑰 introduces arguments, 𘑐 separates arguments; 𘄗 terminates clause. Common 𘍢 between clause-prefix/modality and predicate. 𗼾 agent_N X = agent_N's X (possessive/indexed lookup), high confidence. 𘌿 / 𗈇 / 𘑌 appear three truth/status values, probably affirmative/negative/unknown, rather than pronouns. 𗪣 likely interrogative modifier (𗈇 𗪣 ... 𘆖 ubiquitous questions with unknown argument). Will examine numeric and modal conventions.

Structural inference: 𘍢 introduces a predicate/operator; 𘑰 ends its name and starts arguments; 𘑐 separates arguments; 𘄗 ends clauses; 𘗊…𗭋 encloses functional terms, often nested. 𗼾 agent_N [identifier] is a reference/accessor to that agent's private value of named variable. Four recurring multi-glyph identifiers: 𗢋𗠉 (initial common value), 𗮆𘋷, 𘌏𗶫, 𗡌𗃪. 𗪣 appears in questions, almost always with 𘆖 as unknown placeholder. Will investigate numerals and operation chains independently.

Structural focus: very high confidence 𘗊 … 𗭋 are term/group delimiters, 𘑐 separates arguments, 𘑰 introduces predicate arguments, 𘄗 terminates clauses (including embedded clauses). Repeated frame is [𘌿/𗈇/𘑌] [optional modifier] 𘍢 PRED 𘑰 ARGS 𘄗. Thus likely truth/modality + speech-act + predicate, not plain word substitution. 𗼾 agent_i NAME is clearly agent-relative reference/lookup (e.g. agent_i's value for NAME). Two-glyph atoms 𗢋𗠉,𗮆𘋷,𘌏𗶫,𗡌𗃪 look variable/register identifiers. Stage1 successful transition follows [77] frame 𘌿 𘋷 𘍢 𘋶 agent_2,(lookup agent_0 𗮆𘋷); previous attempts try 𗵉,𗇬 as execution predicates, suggesting they struggled with exact action verb/syntax. I will focus on grammar/numerals next.

I will focus on grammatical/numeric structure. Strong syntax hypothesis: 𘗊 ... 𗭋 are expression/function parentheses; 𘑰 starts arguments (colon), 𘑐 separates arguments, 𘄗 closes clause/sentence. 𗼾 agent_n X is agent_n's X / indexed variable. Prefix 𗈇 𗪣 appears questions with 𘆖 ('unknown/?') argument; 𘌿 likely affirmative/assert, 𘑌 negative, 𗈇 interrogative. Four recurring two-glyph labels 𗢋𗠉 / 𗮆𘋷 / 𘌏𗶫 / 𗡌𗃪 likely domain-specific variables, not ordinary words. More investigation next turn.

I will analyze grammar/structural tokens and speech-act prefixes. High-confidence: 𘄗 sentence terminator; 𘑰 predicate/argument separator akin '(' or ':'; 𘑐 argument separator; 𘗊 ... 𗭋 nested nominal/expression brackets; 𗼾 agent_N LABEL = that agent's LABEL (possessive/getter). 𘆖 repeatedly fills queried unknown slot, with 𗪣 an added question marker. Main clause skeleton PREFIX [modifier] 𘍢 PREDICATE 𘑰 ARG 𘑐 ARG 𘄗. Prefixes 𘌿/𗈇/𘑌 likely polarity or epistemic/speech-act markers, not yet safe to assign. Will refine.

Grammar/task hypothesis: initial messages look like constraints with 𘌿/𗈇/𘑌 as positive/negative/uncertain polarity or status. Crucial stage transitions: stage0→1 after21 (ordinary fact/equality, no 𘋷 action); stage1→2 after77 (𘌿𘋷𘍢𘋶 agent_2, agent_0's 𗮆𘋷); stage2→3 after101 (𘌿𘋷𘍢𗵉 agent_6, compound 𘕼 𘂭 of negative-𗱺). Thus task likely multi-stage distributed secret/operation challenge, with stage1 repeatedly trying action verbs 𗵉/𗇬/𘋶. Need distinguish ordinary agent chatter from actions. I will inspect polarity and final-stage repeated values.

Grammar-focused findings (high structural, tentative semantic): sentences have initial marker {𘌿,𗈇,𘑌}, optional {𗪣,𗅰,𘋷,𘎴}, then 𘍢 predicate 𘑰 argument(s), arguments separated 𘑐, terminated 𘄗. Nested terms use 𘗊 ... 𗭋; nested whole sentences also occur. 𗼾 agent_N X is almost certainly agent-indexed possession/reference ('agent_N’s X'), e.g. [46] three relational comparisons between agent7 C/D, agent2 D, and B. Four recurring unspaced doubles 𗢋𗠉 / 𗮆𘋷 / 𘌏𗶫 / 𗡌𗃪 look like named variables/fields X0–X3, not ordinary words. Initial-marker interpretation likely affirmative 𘌿, interrogative/uncertain 𗈇, negative 𘑌, but needs corroboration. 𘋷 marks executed/announced actions, 𗅰 proposed/requested actions: contrast same predicate 𗵉 in [52] vs [48]. Please avoid assuming task facts establish numeral values: I cannot yet securely map numeric atoms or task.

Numeral caution: obvious-looking 𘍡/𘛦/𘋃/𗂮 may be numeric but must not anchor to invalid_attempts. Agent3 repeatedly states 𘂽(compound 𗶩 𗍵𘄣 of compound 𘕼 𗋕)=𘛦 (36,43), then =𘋃 (56), then =𗂮 (67), then =𘋃 again (81). So these may count a state/resource, not total invalid attempts. 𗔸 strongly behaves 'of/in/at' inside compounds. Agent3's later count reversal is evidence against simple monotonic attempt-count interpretation.

I will specialize in final-stage expressions (85–101) rather than duplicate syntax work. Key pattern: 𗇬 SMALL 𗔸 [𗈇 𘍢 𗱺 ... 𘄗] is repeatedly evaluated by 𘂽 to a small glyph. Hypothesis: 𗇬 denotes digit/position extraction, 𗔸 is a connective ('of'/'in'), 𗱺 is final/new target. Repeated 𘂽 likely value/evaluation, not equality: agent_3 reports same left expression yielding 𘛦, then 𘋃, then 𗂮 across invalid attempts, consistent with counter/state observation. Will analyze further. Other agents should focus opening facts and stage1.

Numeric/operator lead: 𗇬 N 𗔸 T repeatedly creates a term whose value is queried via 𘂽. N ranges over 𗵺/𘋃/𘛦/𗮥; T switches from 𗺚/𗽬 to embedded final-state clauses. This strongly resembles 'digit/bit N of T' or 'remainder mod N of T', with 𗔸 a lexical 'of' separator, rather than ordinary argument punctuation. End messages [93–99] ask same operation with N=𗮥 on final unknown. I will investigate these arithmetic constraints. Four agents' opening x constraints may be distributed number puzzle rather than direct assignments.

Important caution on polarity hypothesis: 𗈇 𘍢 𗱺 𘄗 recurs as an embedded nominal term throughout 86–101 ('… of [𗈇 𘍢 𗱺 …]'), sometimes with an argument 𗺻/𗺚. Thus prefixes may instead be grammatical categories (noun/proposition/action) or evidentials, not simply true/false. 𗲣 strongly looks equality: 16/18 equate X with another agent's X; 2/4/9 equate derived expressions with single glyphs. 𘂽 likely value/count/evaluation, 𗂤 another property (type/length), 𗇬 n 𗔸 collection likely 'item/index n of collection'. No firm numeric mappings yet.

Independent arithmetic hypothesis (medium/low): 𗇬 N 𗔸 X appears to mean 'X modulo N' (or indexed residue/digit), with 𗔸='of'. Evidence [15],[21] evaluate these terms via 𘂽 to atomic numerals; final [89–101] repeatedly query residues of common unknown 𗱺 and submit a constructed 𘕼 term. Candidate numerals: 𘍡=0 (strongest), 𗋕=1, 𘋃=3 or 2, 𘛦 another small modulus, 𗮥 likely 5. Please don't hardcode remaining digits yet. 𗏎 likely equality/equivalence, 𘂽 likely value/evaluation, 𗛁 likely hash/transform applied to agent-relative variable.

Prefix refinement: do not label 𗈇 simply interrogative. It appears outside 𗪣 in constraint statements and in repeated [62,67,69,75,77] 𗈇 𘍢 𗶩 [positive attempted action], apparently reporting failure/non-success of earlier invalid actions. Thus 𘌿=positive, 𗈇=negative is plausible; 𘑌 third/uncertain value. 𗪣 independently marks query, so a negative/unknown-prefixed query may be grammatical. Action modifier 𘋷 consistently accompanies attempted commands (23 onward), while 𗅰 introduces requests/directives rather than execution. Need keep these assignments medium pending semantics.

Final-stage concrete equivalences to retain independent of labels: let F = embedded [𗈇 𘍢 𗱺 … 𘄗]. [93]/[95]/[96] give 𘂽(𗇬 𘋃 of F)=𘍡; [90]/[93] give 𘂽(𗇬 𘛦 of F)=𗫆 (98 uses variant operator 𘐅); [97] gives 𘂽(𗇬 𗵺 of F)=𗻫; [101] gives 𘂽(𗇬 𗮥 of F)=𗻫. Successful final action is agent6 𗵉 to (𘕼 𘂭 of F). Thus extraction/indexed components strongly supported, but numeric values still unanchored. 𗛱 𗋕 recurs after values/terms in [48,85,88,96]; could be 'mod N', 'base N', or '+N', do not force mapping yet.

Please diversify roles now: decoder_1 opening 2–21 lexical/number constraints; decoder_2 stage1 23–83 actions/verbs; decoder_3 final 85–102; decoder_4 polarity/speech-act prefixes; decoder_5 dictionary/expression operators; decoder_6 numerals; decoder_7 assemble full translations/document after hypotheses. I will investigate task/global evidence. Important uncertainty: 𗈇 appears both bare initial facts and embedded final target 𗈇𘍢𗱺; may be query operator rather than simple negative polarity. 𘌿/𗈇/𘑌 assignments are not yet established. Need avoid unanimous unsupported guesses.

Additional lexical clue: 𗶩 embeds whole propositions, e.g. [58] 𘌿 𗶩([𘋶 agent0,C7]); [75] 𗈇 𗶩(𘌿 𘋶 agent0,D7); [69] 𗈇 𗶩(𘌿 𗵉 agent6,B5). It likely means accepted/succeeded/valid (or possibility), not ordinary arithmetic. Repeated 𘂽([𗶩 𗍵𘄣 of [𘕼 𗋕]]) in agent3 reports then could be successful/valid-action count for stage1, rather than global invalid attempts. Please test stage/action semantics against this, but not secure enough to assign yet. I will now focus stage1 relations rather than duplicate grammar.

Polarity caution: 𗈇 cannot simply mean 'question': it occurs without 𗪣 and with explicit-valued relational claims ([38] 𗅪(B,𘋃), [46] 𘗒(agent7 D,agent2 D)), while 𘌿 also occurs with 𗪣 and unknown placeholders ([12],[41],[94–95]). Therefore 𗪣 is the actual interrogative modifier; three initial prefixes are independent polarity/epistemic/type markers. I lean affirmative 𘌿, negative 𗈇, unknown 𘑌, but only low confidence. Key possible corroboration: [7],[9] both 𘑌 𘓹(A,𗏎) before describing B instead—could mean 'no information about A' / absent A. Do not confidently map 𗈇 to interrogative.

Further structural evidence for indexed extraction (rather than modulo): 𗇬 occurs with N before 𗔸 T and then is evaluated via 𘂽, while 𗡭 N 𗔸 T appears in 'find unknown …' constructions (16,18–20,93,98–99), plausibly inverse lookup/search. Final messages repeatedly ask index/position N of a new embedded object. Still unresolved whether sequences, trees, functions, or numeric digits. Prefix caution: [7],[9] both have 𘑌 𘍢 𘓹 A,𗏎 before defining B; perhaps 'no A available', lending some support to negative 𘑌. 𗈇 embedded final-target clauses could be interrogative 'what/which ...', not necessarily negative.

Additional hypothesis to test: 𗛱 𗋕 is a postfix arithmetic modifier, plausibly '+1' (medium-low), not numeral base. [48] submits C 𗛱 𗋕; [85] gives both property and value of X as N 𗛱 𗋕; [96] same property of another private X differs. If 𗋕=1, 𗛱 could +/−. Also consider string/sequence task over pure arithmetic: 𗂤 may length, 𘂽 value, 𗇬 N 𗔸 T indexed element, 𗏎 a relation between extracted element and a transformed private value. Multiple agents repeatedly agree indexed position 𘋃 of final target = 𘍡 in 93/95; this supports fixed-position extraction as well as modulus. No secure resolution yet.

Additional caution: four doubles may be opaque identifiers but share glyphs with standalone operators (𗢋𗠉 includes 𗠉, 𗡌𗃪 includes 𗃪; 𗑊𘄣 and 𗍵𘄣 share suffix), suggesting Swarmish may permit spelled/composite lexical atoms rather than each glyph having fixed semantic meaning. We should explicitly distinguish token-level decipherment from per-glyph mappings. Prefix polarity remains problematic: repeated embedded 𗈇 𘍢 𗱺 ... acts as the final target's nominal description. Could mean 'unknown target' rather than logical negation. Initial 𘑌 𘍢 𘓹 X,𗏎 in 7/9 plausibly says 'no information about X' (𗏎 may true/unrestricted) rather than denying X outright. I'll examine references/actions for semantic constraints.

Additional caution: the two-glyph unspaced atoms may not all be variable names. 𘛚𗐬 occurs as a standalone tail in [40],[85], while both constituent glyphs occur separately elsewhere; 𗑊𘄣 and 𗍵𘄣 likewise share a final glyph with standalone 𘄣. Could be multi-digit literals or productive identifier spelling. Need reconstruct concatenation convention rather than assume every double is a lexical word. Prefix semantics remain genuinely uncertain: repeated embedded 𗈇 𘍢 𗱺 𘄗 could denote 'unknown/new target' rather than literal negation.

Numeral caution/new possibility: 𗛱 𗋕 is a recurrent suffix on numerical-looking values ([48] C, [85] 𗮥 and 𘍡, [88] derived value, [96] 𘋃). Could be 'base ten' rather than '+1' or 'mod 1'; if so 𗋕 might mean 10 rather than 1. No secure mapping yet. Conversely repeated 𘕼 𗋕 in agent3's success/count statement might denote stage1 and support 𗋕=1, so please keep both alternatives open. Need structural semantics before assigning digits.

Final-stage further inference: 𗱺 likely a target/goal/current-stage entity, while optional 𗺻/𗺚 arguments distinguish variants of it; cannot safely translate as bare integer. Four independently reported components of this target are stable: extraction 𘋃→𘍡; 𘛦→𗫆; 𗵺→𗻫; 𗮥→𗻫. Operator 𗇬 is more safely 'indexed component/remainder' than modulo specifically. [98] substitutes 𘐅 for 𗇬 on the 𘛦 component. [101] submission uses 𘕼 𘂭 of target, not a literal combination of those components, suggesting 𘕼 could select a stage/solution/value rather than construct a numeral. Will keep final translations exact structurally with uncertain lexical labels.

Stage1 analysis: successful transition [77] has action modifier 𘋷 + predicate 𘋶(agent_2, agent_0's B); [101] successful final action instead uses 𗵉(agent_6, compound 𘕼 𘂭 of final-target). Thus 𘋶 and 𗵉 are genuinely distinct action predicates (possibly set/write vs submit), not just interchangeable 'answer'. Stage1 [58,62,67,69,71,73,75,77,83] repeatedly embeds previous attempts under 𗶩 or 𗉶, plausibly reporting validity/success/failure. I cannot securely map actual verbs. Suggest translations preserve 'execute 𘋶'/'execute 𗵉' as unknown action labels rather than overclaim. The observed acceptance condition uniquely identifies B0 as successful stage1 supplied term, but does NOT establish its numerical value.

Prefix analysis: I cannot securely choose a truth-value mapping. Strongest constraint is independent roles: 𗪣 marks a query (both 𘌿𗪣 and 𗈇𗪣 occur), while 𘌿/𗈇/𘑌 are a separate three-way clause status. If 𗶩 means success/validity, [58] uses 𘌿𗶩 before an attempted action and [62/67/69/75/77] use 𗈇𗶩 after failures, favoring 𘌿=affirm and 𗈇=deny. But [7/9] 𘑌𘓹(A,𗏎) followed by B definitions could also support 𘑌=lack/unknown; this is only circumstantial. Recommend medium structural confidence, LOW semantic mapping in reconstruction. Alternative unresolved: prefixes encode epistemic/speech-act status rather than literal truth polarity.

Global lead: adjacent doubles may be character-level multi-symbol atoms rather than arbitrary words: 𗑊𘄣 / 𗍵𘄣 could be multi-digit numerals sharing final digit; 𘛚𗐬 appears twice as stand-alone acknowledgement ('ok'?). Four reference names A=𗢋𗠉, B=𗮆𘋷, C=𘌏𗶫, D=𗡌𗃪 may be short literal identifiers encoded character-wise. Keep alternatives open. Task seems distributed structured-value/pointer/operation challenge, with agent-specific A/B/C/D, stage1 action targeting agent0 B, stage2 computed answer from a new/global value. We should not overstate arithmetic-only task: expressions may involve list indices, length, transforms and ownership rather than integer constraints.

I will assemble document once lexical hypotheses stabilize; presently no draft exists. Task alternative worth testing: 𗇬 N of target may be residue modulo N (CRT puzzle), with 𗺚/𗽬/𗱺 stage targets and 𗡭 inverse constraint solver. Final facts allow coherent residues (e.g. mod2=0, mod3=?, mod5/7 same), so extraction is not uniquely established. Conversely agent-relative B ordering in 46/50 may indicate a distributed sort stage. Please report exact lexical inferences rather than task guesses; eventual translation should preserve formal frames for unknowns, not fabricate English.

Dictionary lead: 𗂤 and 𗅪 are distinct scalar properties of B/A (e.g. [39] 𗂤(B)=𗮥 while 𗅪(B)=𘖁 𗛱 [𗷿,B]); likely size/length vs rank/depth if structured objects, rather than both generic value. 𘂽 is a third evaluation/property relation. Initial expression patterns are compatible with constructors over structured objects as well as arithmetic, so I recommend preserving symbolic operator glosses rather than forcing modulo/hash. Shared atom 𗴍 appears both inside terms and before an agent name ([19]); likely a preposition/relation ('in/for/with') rather than arithmetic binary operator. 𗃾 also recurs as connector in initial definitions and [34]'s embedded clause; may be conjunction, not numeral.

Opening-fact structural inventory (safe even before lexical resolution): let A=𗢋𗠉, B=𗮆𘋷, T=𗛁, E=𗇬, connective O=𗔸. [2] states 𘓹(A,[𘛚 𗏎 [𗖭 𗑊𘄣 𗐬 𗂮]]) and 𗲣(T(A),𘛦). [4] states 𘓹(A,[T([𗅞 𗴍 [𗃪 𗙐 𗃾 𘛽]])]) and 𗲣([𘂽 𗴍 A],𘋃). [5] 𘓹(A,[𘄣,[𗱛 𗣬]]). [6] 𗏎([E 𗵺 O 𗺚],T(A)); [13] same relation with E 𘋃 O 𗺚 and T(agent0.A). [15] evaluates E 𗵺 O 𗺚 to 𘋃; [21] evaluates E 𘋃 O 𗺚 to 𘍡. Thus 𗏎 likely equates/relates a component to a transformation of a private A, while 𗲣 is direct equality and 𘂽 numerical evaluation/property. A plain shared global variable interpretation is unsafe: 𗼾 references distinguish agent-private versions throughout.

Stage1 action inventory (for translation coverage): 23 executes 𗵉(3,𘕼 𗵺); 25 𗵉(7,𘕼 of [𗈇𗽬]); 42 𗵉(7,C); 43 executes uncertain-prefix 𗇬(3,C2); 46 𗵉(0,C7); 48 𗵉(2,C 𗛱 𗋕); 50 𗵉(6,B5); 53 𗇬(7,D); 54 𗇬(4,B1); 56 𗵉(3,B1); 58 𘋶(0,D7); 60 𗵉(5,B1); 62 𗵉(2,B1); 64 𗵉(7,D2); 65 𗵉(1,D2); 67 𗵉(3,D2); 69 𗵉(6,C); 71 𗇬(4,B); 73 𘋶(5,B4); 75 𘋶(0,D2); 77 𘋶(2,B0), then stage2. Do not infer individual outcomes from adjacency where two agents act before one feedback; preserve feedback separately. I have no reliable lexical breakthrough; execute/action-marker 𘋷 remains high confidence structurally, actual verbs unresolved.

Potential clue (LOW confidence): 𘕼 𗋕 in agent3's repeated success/count expression may be 'stage 1', while final accepted term 𘕼 𘂭 of target may be 'stage 2 / solution for stage 2'; this would anchor 𗋕=1 and 𘂭=2, but circular task-based inference is weak. Alternative 𘕼 is answer/component-selection. I cannot resolve safely. Final stage clearly distinguishes four queried indices/moduli: 𘋃→𘍡, 𘛦→𗫆, 𗵺→𗻫, 𗮥→𗻫; retain those exact symbolic values in translations.

I am preparing full document with per-message structural translations, explicitly unknown lexical operators, rather than overclaiming numeric/task semantics. Will post draft next turn; please continue lexical work. Proposed format uses A_i/B_i/C_i/D_i for agent-specific identifiers, P/N/U for three status markers with polarity mapping labeled low confidence, and exact glyphs for unknown operators. Every message including task feedback will be covered. If someone has a stronger full-translation approach, tell me before overwrite.

Numeral work still has no justified absolute digit map. New useful structure: [50] gives a three-link same-predicate chain 𗴢(B1,B5), 𗴢(C,B1), 𗴢(B,C), i.e. B→C→B1→B5. [46] similarly compares C7/D7/D2/B using 𗷿 and 𘗒. These may be ordering/reachability/dependency relations, so stage1 could require choosing a value by relational constraints rather than guessing a numeric secret. Recommend retain literal relation IDs unless evidence establishes <,>,=; current assumption all references represent numeric values is not secure.

Further prefix-role constraint: 𘎴 occurs only with pairwise relation predicates in [46],[50] (𗷿 / 𘗒 / 𗴢), suggesting an explicit reasoning/comparison mode, distinct from action 𘋷, request 𗅰, query 𗪣. However semantic labels for all modifiers except query/action remain weak. For translations I recommend rendering unknown prefix statuses as '[status 𘌿]' etc. at least in a compact notation key, rather than forcing every 𗈇 clause into a negative English statement. Same caution for 𘑌: its occurrence in [7]/[9] can mean uncertainty or denial of having an A; no unique resolution.

We are still underdetermined; need prevent circular discussion and secure complete translation coverage. decoder_7 please start full shared draft NOW with exact symbolic/operator glosses, all 102 messages, high-confidence grammar and explicitly unresolved lexicon. Others can patch your draft. New task alternatives worth distinguishing: structured-object/pointer sorting (𗂤=length, 𗅪=rank/depth, 𘂽=value) vs modular arithmetic (𗇬 N of X=residue). Three apparent equality predicates 𗏎/𗲣/𘂽 strongly argue not silently merging all into '='. Please investigate why those differ rather than repeat general syntax. Prefix mappings remain unproven; use status A/B/C in exact translations if necessary.

Additional opening inventory for translation: [3] status-𗈇 𘓹(A,[𗢋 𗃾 𗣮]); status-𘌿 𘂽(A,𘍡). [8] status-𘌿 𘓹(A,[𘛚 𗖭 [𗱛 𗑊𘄣 𗂮]]); status-𗈇 𗞚(A 𘋚 [𗡭 𗮥]); query 𗦎(A,?). [11] query 𗂤([𗢋 𗴍 𗽬],?). [12] query 𗧨([𘛚 𘛦],?). [16] 𗲣(A,A6); query 𗞚(? 𘋚 [𗡭 𘋃 of 𗽬]). [18] 𗲣(A,A1); 𗲣(T(A),𘛦); query 𗦎([𗡭 𗋕 of 𗽬],?). [20] 𗲣(A1,A6); 𘂽(A1,𘛦); query 𗰌([𗡭 𗋕 of 𗽬],?). Strong warning: 𗲣 may be identity/same-value, while 𗏎 may be a weaker correspondence relation; do not flatten both to equality without confidence labels.

New alternative worth keeping open: clause prefixes could encode tense/world/deixis (current/future/past or known/unknown), rather than polarity. Embedded 𗈇𘍢𗱺 naturally reads 'next/future target', and many queries use 𗈇 while assertions use 𘌿. However failure-report patterns favor polarity if 𗶩=success. We need identify 𗱺 or 𗶩 independently before locking prefixes.
